title: Armed Suspect Arrested Outside White House After Allegedly Threatening President Trump
snippet: Authorities arrested a Venezuelan national near the White House complex late Thursday after finding him inside a stolen pickup truck packed with an AR-15, a MAC-10, and ammunition.
content:
U.S. Secret Service officers arrested a Venezuelan national late Thursday night after discovering him parked near the White House complex inside a stolen pickup truck filled with high-powered firearms and ammunition, federal authorities said.

The suspect, identified in court records as Ronny Guanipa-Chrinos, was spotted by a patrolling officer shortly before midnight sitting in a blue Ford F-150 along Constitution Avenue. When the officer approached the vehicle and inquired whether he was carrying any weapons, Guanipa-Chrinos reportedly nodded in agreement and made a finger-gun gesture.

Arsenal Recovered from Stolen Truck

Upon searching the stolen vehicle, law enforcement officers uncovered a serious stash of weaponry, including an AR-15 semi-automatic rifle, a MAC-10 machine pistol, a Glock 43x handgun, and dozens of rounds of live ammunition, according to a criminal complaint affidavit filed in D.C. Superior Court.

After stepping out of the truck, Guanipa-Chrinos attempted to explain the situation to investigators using Google Translate. He allegedly claimed he took one of the guns from an individual who had attempted to kill him.

Alleged Threats to the President

According to statements released by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Guanipa-Chrinos told officers that he began "hearing voices in his head" commanding him to travel to Washington, D.C., to kill President Donald Trump.

DHS records indicate that Guanipa-Chrinos is an undocumented immigrant who originally crossed into the United States through Texas in 2024.

Charges and Court Appearance

Guanipa-Chrinos appeared in D.C. Superior Court on Friday to face multiple charges, including carrying a pistol without a license, carrying a rifle without a license, unauthorized use of a vehicle, and receiving stolen property. A judge ordered him held without bond pending further legal proceedings.
